title: A 2001-2019 dengue temperature curve gave half the possible 2020-2024 forecast gain in Brazilian municipalities, but its 20-26 C slope rose from near 0 to 0.8-1.0 per C after 2012
abstract: Question: is the dengue temperature response of Childs et al. (2025, PNAS), fitted to data up to 2019, stable enough to forecast? Approach: we fitted their Poisson panel model (cubic temperature at lags 1-3, municipality, state-year and state-month fixed effects) to OpenDengue V1.3.1 probable cases in 5,528 Brazilian municipalities, with CRU TS 4.09 and Berkeley Earth temperature. We tested 2020-2024 data that the original study did not use. Results: in 2001-2019 the shape repeated, but the peak was 25.7 C with CRU and 27.75 C with Berkeley Earth (published: 27.8 C). The published cool-side doubling (slope about 0.69 per C at 15-20 C) did not occur: national slopes at 16-18 C were at most +0.33. The fixed 2001-2019 curve gave 55-56% of the deviance gain of a 2020-2024 refit (8.2% against 14.5%). A placebo that used temperatures from 5 years earlier made the fit worse (-6.9%). But the curve was not stable. The slope at 20-26 C was near zero in 2001-2012 and 0.72-1.05 per C in 2013-2019 and 2020-2024 (z up to 8.7). A 2001-2012 curve made 2013-2019 forecasts worse than no temperature term. A 2013-2019 curve gave skill 0.69 for 2020-2024. Regions had different slopes at equal temperature, and future-temperature leads had small slopes. Limitations: Brazil only; monthly CRU at municipal seats instead of daily ERA5; a 2014 change from monthly to weekly reporting; 27 state clusters. Code, plan, coefficients, curves and figures are bundled; case and climate data stay external.

display.caption: A: dengue temperature response (log incidence relative to 24.5 C, lags 1-3 summed) for Brazilian municipalities in 2001-2019 (blue) and 2020-2024 (orange), CRU TS 4.09 temperature, 95% bands from state-clustered SEs. The dotted line is the published 27.8 C peak. B: slope of the response by period. The slope at 20-26 C is near zero in 2001-2012 and about 0.8-1.0 per C in 2013-2019 and 2020-2024. The dotted line is the published cool-side doubling (0.69 per C).

Percent Poisson deviance reduction in 2020-2024 against a model without temperature, nationally and by macro-region. Grey: curve refitted on 2020-2024 (upper bound). Blue: fixed 2001-2019 curve. Green: fixed 2013-2019 curve (exploratory). Orange: placebo, the 2001-2019 curve applied to temperatures from 5 years earlier. A: state x month fixed effects as in Childs et al.; B: municipality x month fixed effects (year-to-year anomalies only).

Identification checks, response slopes per C, 2001-2019 unless stated. A: municipality x month fixed effects give the same curve as state x month fixed effects. B: lead placebo; temperatures 1-2 months in the future have small slopes of their own. C: slopes by macro-region (2 x 2-degree block-cluster SEs); regions differ at the same temperature.
